speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what is the basis for the latest increase in electricity tariffs and gas prices; (b) whether the consumption of electricity and gas has increased as more residents work from home; and (c) whether increased development in alternative sources of energy has helped reduce the overall cost of electricity for consumers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: I have circulated a chart which has been placed on Members' seats, so that it can show clearly my explanation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: However, the electricity and gas tariffs in the third and fourth quarters of 2020 still remain lower than in the first quarter of 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: And the prices, the tariffs are amongst the lowest since January 2018.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: So, the prices for  this last quarter that has just passed, are still amongst the lowest since January 2018.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Around 47% of all households will not be affected by the new tariff prices because they have already switched to the Open Electricity Market.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Alternative energy sources today constitute a small proportion of our power generation because of our natural geographical limitations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: However, our Government is actively partnering industry partners and industry players to deploy more solar power to enhance our energy resilience, our competitiveness as well as longer term sustainability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We aim to increase our solar capacity by five-fold.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: And we hope that that will contribute to around 3% of our energy consumption in 2030.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Consumers who are interested to procure solar power can do so by engaging our local solar companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Moving on to households’ average monthly electricity and town gas consumption, and if we looked at the consumption from April to July 2020 – this is for the monthly average electricity and town gas consumption – it was 16% for electricity and 34% for town gas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: So, 16% and 34% higher compared to the same period last year respectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: It is a difficult point to note on discussion, so, I want to repeat that: households' average monthly electricity and town gas consumption from April to July 2020, was 16% and 34% higher compared to the same period last year, respectively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is mainly due to the fact that Singaporeans spent more time at home during the circuit breaker period and during the early stages of our phased re-opening, as part of our national efforts to manage local community transmissions of COVID-19.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We have also provided Singaporean households with more support for their utility bills this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Every household with at least one Singapore Citizen received a one-off $100 Solidarity Utilities Credit in their July or August SP Group utility bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The GST Voucher – U-Save that eligible households receive has also been doubled this year through a one-off GST Voucher – U-Save Special Payment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Eligible HDB households with five or more members also received a first tranche of further GST Voucher – U-Save rebates of between $60 and $100 per household in October, with a second tranche to be disbursed in January 2021.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Before this year, the annual amount of GST Voucher – U-Save that households in 1- and 2-room HDB flats received was equivalent to about three to four months of their utilities bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Those living in 3- and 4-room HDB flats received support equivalent to about one to two months of their utilities bills on average.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We want to make sure that the support is given to families most in need and hence, the higher quantum in terms of the GST Voucher – U-Save that the households in 1- and 2-room HDB flats received compared to those in 3- and 4-room flats.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: With the additional support this year, households in 1- and 2-room HDB flats will receive support equivalent to at least six to eight months of their utilities bills on average.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: And households living in 3- and 4-room HDB flats will receive support equivalent to at least two to four months of their utilities bills.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, such headlines do cause anxiety, especially during this period where the environment is really difficult and indeed, residents have consumed more electricity because of working from home, staying at home more often.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, I want to ask the Minister how we can better communicate this, so that we do not cause unnecessary alarm or concern when residents see the headline number of 9.3% increase.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: The second question is, the Minister mentioned that the tariffs affected 53% of the households and the remaining 47% households are not affected.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: Given the unsettling effect of price changes quarter-to-quarter, would the Ministry perhaps use this opportunity to encourage more Singaporeans to go on the fixed price plan, so that there is some certainty; whether that can be pushed out to more residents to adopt and to sign up; whether there are other incentives that can encourage our Singaporeans to sign up as well?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In terms of the communications to the households, Mr Speaker, Sir, if you look at the breakdown of all of the utilities bills that SP and some of the retailer send out to the households, these are detailed breakdown in terms of the tariffs charged.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At the same time, in terms of the rebates, many of the households in the 1-, 2-, 3-room and 4-room flats would have gotten their rebates.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We believe that that has been communicated quite adequately across.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Of course, in terms of communications, we will find ways and means in which we can continue to improve and further fine-tune how to educate many of our households in terms of managing their utilities bills.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: One of the key initiatives as a result of these fluctuations or volatility of prices, it is important for us to note that our tariffs are based on what is the prevalent crude oil price.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Ninety-five percent of our electricity is generated by the generating companies or gencos using piped and liquified natural gas from overseas.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is in the interest of many people to switch to the Open Market retailers, to switch onto some of these packaged price plans, as what was surmised by the hon Member Mr Liang Eng Hwa.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because I think in the ensuing quarters ahead, there will continue to be more volatility and fluctuations to happen.
